mechanism: Torsemide causes hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia which increase QT prolongation risk; promethazine has anticholinergic effects and can cause orthostatic hypotension, compounded by torsemide-induced volume depletion.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (K+, Mg2+) regularly, assess QTc interval if available, counsel on orthostatic precautions, and consider alternative antihistamine with lower anticholinergic burden if possible.
